Final report

Trishuli Flood Damage Mapping — Final Report

Track B — Multimodal AI Hackathon 2026

Post-event damage assessment for the 26 August 2026 Trishuli–Bhote Koshi flash flood, Rasuwa District, Nepal.

Executive summary

We built a complete, reproducible pipeline to map flood extent, building damage, and hospital access for the 26 August 2026 GLOF that struck the Trishuli / Bhote Koshi corridor. The pipeline ingests free Sentinel-1 SAR, DEM, OpenStreetMap, and Copernicus EMS Rapid Mapping reference data and produces flood masks, affected-infrastructure layers, hospital-reachability metrics, and a trained U-Net segmentation model.

The central finding is negative and important: the Sentinel-1 pre/post pair available for this event does not contain the GLOF signal. Two independent methods — a physics-based SAR change detector and a U-Net segmentation model trained on Sen1Floods11 — both return effectively zero flood extent on the Rasuwa corridor. We report this as a substantive result rather than tuning thresholds to noise.

Headline numbers:

Metric Value Interpretation
Sentinel-1 VV change at AOI01 −0.31 dB within noise (GLOF would show −5 to −10 dB)
U-Net predicted flood fraction, Rasuwa 0.000 model independently confirms no signal
U-Net val IoU (Sen1Floods11) 0.523 trained model is real, generalizes
U-Net proxy-Himalaya IoU 0.554 monsoon-subcontinent chips
EMSR927 damage-point recall 0.000 all four AOIs
Our "flooded" buildings 61,977 16× overcount vs EMSR927's 3,816

1. Study area and event

On 26 August 2026, a flash flood reportedly triggered by a Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) struck Rasuwa District, Nepal. The Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers, which drain south from the Nepal–China border through Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Chitwan, carried a debris-laden surge downstream. Copernicus EMS Rapid Mapping was activated (EMSR927) and mapped building damage across four Areas of Interest:

AOI Locality District Lat / Lon Damage points
01 Syapru Besi Rasuwa 28.17 N, 85.34 E 433
02 Timure Rasuwa 28.26 N, 85.37 E 431
03 Bidur Nuwakot 27.93 N, 85.15 E 2,343
05 Phosretar (Chitwan edge) 27.83 N, 85.02 E 609

Total EMSR927 damage points: 3,816 (2,813 Destroyed, 354 Damaged, 649 Possibly damaged).

Study area bbox: (84.50, 27.40, 86.00, 28.40) — the Trishuli corridor from Rasuwa to the Terai, projected to EPSG:32645 at 30 m.

2. Data

Source Purpose Snapshot
Sentinel-1 GRD SAR change detection 2026-08-16 (pre) / 2026-08-28 (post)
Copernicus DEM Slope masking n/a
OpenStreetMap Infrastructure, settlements, hospitals 2026-09-30
Sen1Floods11 v1.1 U-Net training published dataset
Copernicus EMSR927 Validation reference activation 2026-08-26

Sentinel-1 pairing. Two products per date on relative orbit 85, ascending, 12-day gap:

  • Pre: S1D_IW_GRDH_1SDV_20260816T122116_…_B057 (southern) and …_20260816T122141_…_C3AB (northern)
  • Post: S1D_IW_GRDH_1SDV_20260828T122116_…_C523 (southern) and …_20260828T122141_…_01B4 (northern)

Both northern and southern frames are needed — the SAR swath is a diagonal parallelogram and Rasuwa falls in the gap between single-frame footprints. Orbit invariants are verified by src/processing/align_v2_checks.py before any alignment runs.

3. Methods

3.1 Sentinel-1 preprocessing

Raw SAFE measurement TIFFs are not georeferenced. We geocode them from the GCPs in annotation/*.xml using gdal_translate -gcp followed by gdalwarp -t_srs EPSG:32645 -tr 30 30, producing one north-up 30 m raster per polarization per frame (src/processing/geocode_s1.py).

Pre and post frames are then merged, converted to dB, and matched to the reference DEM grid (src/processing/align.py). Amplitude-to-dB conversion uses 20·log10(DN) − 60; zero DN is treated as nodata.

3.2 Flood detection

src/processing/flood_detect_v2.py implements:

  1. Lee speckle filter (7×7, ENL=4)
  2. Dual-pol change image: d = 0.5·(VV_post − VV_pre) + 0.5·(VH_post − VH_pre)
  3. Adaptive threshold on the 5th percentile of d, clipped to [−3.5, −1.5] dB
  4. Slope mask (reject > 12°)
  5. Permanent-water mask (pre-event VV < −18 dB OR VH < −22 dB)
  6. Morphological opening + minimum patch size 20 px
  7. Output: data/processed/flood_mask.tif (uint8, binary)

3.3 Damage assessment

src/processing/damage_v2.py intersects OSM buildings, roads, and bridges with the flood and debris masks, writing:

  • outputs/affected_buildings.gpkg
  • outputs/affected_roads.geojson
  • outputs/affected_bridges.geojson
  • outputs/impact_summary.json

3.4 Hospital reachability

src/processing/cutoff_v2.py builds a weighted road graph in EPSG:32645, snaps settlements and hospitals to the nearest graph node (≤1 km), and runs multi-source Dijkstra from all hospitals. Pre-flood graph uses all OSM roads; post-flood graph removes road segments whose midpoint lies inside the flood mask. Output: outputs/cutoff_settlements.json with pre/post distances and detour factors.

3.5 U-Net segmentation

src/modeling/train_segmentation.py trains a 4-encoder / 3-decoder U-Net with skip connections (2-channel dual-pol input, ~7.8 M parameters) on Sen1Floods11 v1.1 (252 train / 89 val). 20 epochs, Adam lr=1e-3, cosine LR schedule, BCE-with-logits loss computed only on valid (non--1) label pixels. Best checkpoint saved to outputs/flood_unet.pt.

3.6 Validation

Two independent reference checks:

  • src/validation/emsr927_comparison.py — rasterizes EMSR927 builtUpP damage points and observedEventA landslide polygons onto the flood-mask grid, clips to AOI, and computes damage-point recall and landslide overlap.
  • src/validation/damage_sanity_check.py — compares our impact_summary.json counts against EMSR927 per-AOI damage totals.

4. Results

4.1 The flood mask does not contain the GLOF

The strongest single diagnostic is per-AOI backscatter change, saved to outputs/diagnostics/aoi_backscatter_diagnostics.json:

AOI VV pre (dB) VV post (dB) change (dB) combined p05 (dB)
01 Syapru Besi −13.86 −14.04 −0.31 −1.40
02 Timure −12.80 −12.54 +0.18 −0.98
03 Bidur −15.50 −14.79 +0.41 +0.00
05 Phosretar −14.95 −14.60 +0.21 +0.00

A real GLOF over water produces a −5 to −10 dB drop in VV backscatter. We observe −0.3 to +0.4 dB. The signal is not there.

Four mechanisms plausibly contribute:

  1. Temporal mismatch. GLOFs drain in hours; the 2-day post-event gap (2026-08-26 event → 2026-08-28 acquisition) likely missed standing water.
  2. Radar geometry. The ascending pass illuminates the Trishuli valley obliquely; deep N–S gorges are partly in radar shadow.
  3. Spatial resolution. At 30 m, the ~30–50 m wide Bhote Koshi channel is under-resolved; each pixel mixes water with bank rock.
  4. Debris and vegetation. Post-GLOF debris flows leave rough surfaces that scatter radar rather than specularly reflecting.

4.2 Independent confirmation from the U-Net

The trained U-Net was tiled across the Rasuwa SAR change images and predicted zero flood pixels (234 tiles, flood fraction = 0.000). Two independent methods reaching the same conclusion strongly supports the negative result.

4.3 The U-Net itself works

Split IoU F1 Precision Recall
Sen1Floods11 full val (89 chips) 0.574 0.729 0.723 0.735
Proxy-Himalaya, India + Pakistan (20 chips) 0.554 0.713 0.685 0.744

The proxy evaluation is only 0.02 IoU below the full val — the model generalizes rather than memorizing. It is a real segmentation model; it simply sees no flood because there is none in the data.

4.4 EMSR927 validation returns zero

AOI Destroyed recall Landslide overlap Flood in AOI
01 Syapru Besi 0.000 0.000 0.00 km²
02 Timure 0.000 0.000 0.00 km²
03 Bidur 0.000 0.003 0.14 km²
05 Phosretar 0.051 0.076 0.83 km²

Zero destroyed-building recall at the two Rasuwa AOIs. The 0.83 km² in AOI05 is monsoon-terrain noise, not the GLOF — the same 47 km² mask scatters across the entire mosaic.

4.5 Damage assessment: 16× overcount

Metric Our pipeline EMSR927 Ratio
Flooded buildings 61,977 — —
EMSR927 damage points (all grades) — 3,816 —
Overcount factor — — 16.2×

The damage pipeline is mechanically correct — the flood mask driving it is not.

4.6 Hospital reachability

Metric Value
Settlements 1,565
Hospitals 1,002
Reachable pre-flood 1,561
Reachable post-flood 1,561
Settlements becoming unreachable 0
Detour > 3× 13 (11 sub-kilometre artifacts, 1 real 43× detour)

Because the flood mask removes only 4.7% of road segments and no settlement lost connectivity entirely, the cut-off conclusions are dominated by noise. The one real signal — a settlement 1.66 km from a hospital becoming 70.9 km away — is plausibly a bridge loss over the Trishuli.

5. Limitations

5.1 The event is not observable in the input data. This is the dominant limitation. Sentinel-1 ascending 30 m imagery acquired 2 days after a fast-draining GLOF cannot resolve the event. We demonstrate this quantitatively in §4.1–4.2 rather than tuning thresholds to noise. Optical imagery (Sentinel-2, Planet) or higher-resolution SAR (TerraSAR-X, COSMO-SkyMed) would be required to map the flood surface directly.

5.2 EMSR927 GRA products contain no flood extent layer. The activation mapped building damage and mass movements, not water. Our validation is therefore proxy-based (damage-point recall and landslide overlap), not a direct IoU against a flood reference.

5.3 OSM snapshot is post-event. The buildings and roads used for impact assessment were downloaded 2026-09-30, five weeks after the event. Any post-flood OSM edits (new buildings, reclassified roads) contaminate the pre-flood baseline. This affects the damage assessment but not the satellite analysis.

5.4 30 m resolution limits bridge-level accuracy. The Bhote Koshi channel is ~30–50 m wide. Even with a correct SAR signal, pixel-level classification of the channel would be marginal.

5.5 U-Net trained on out-of-distribution data. Sen1Floods11 contains no Himalayan scenes. The proxy evaluation on India+Pakistan chips is the closest available, but it does not establish the model's performance on steep mountain valleys.

5.6 The debris mask is nearly all speckle. The final debris layer (111,874 px) collapses to ~2,000 px after strict minimum-patch filtering — i.e. the pre-morphology debris class is dominated by noise. This is a tuning issue in flood_detect_v2.py and would need addressing on real event data.

5.7 Hospital reachability assumes road-network completeness. OSM road coverage in rural Rasuwa is incomplete; missing minor tracks may over-estimate cut-off.

6. Recommendations

  1. Re-acquire this event with different data. Optical (Sentinel-2 L2A, PlanetScope) would capture post-GLOF sediment plumes directly. High-resolution SAR (TerraSAR-X stripmap) would resolve the channel.
  2. Widen the Sentinel-1 search. A descending pass (relOrbit 121 or 19, visible in the catalogue) would illuminate the valley from the opposite direction and might capture water before it drains. Same-day imagery (Sentinel-1 acquisition ≈ event time) would be ideal — none existed for this event.
  3. For future GLOF events, task optical assets immediately. Rapid mapping windows are 24–72 hours. Sentinel-1's 12-day repeat is too slow for GLOF hydrology.
  4. Fix the debris-mask classifier. The pre-morphology debris count (475k → 111k → ~2k) reveals a threshold that catches speckle. A dual-threshold or GLCM-texture approach would be more robust.
  5. Replace the OSM snapshot for pre-event analysis. Use a 2026-07 Geofabrik PBF and rebuild the buildings layer.

7. Reproducibility

Every stage runs from the repo root with pinned dependencies (requirements.txt). Full pipeline:

bash run_all.sh

Checks:

python -m pytest tests/ -q     # 14 passing
python src/processing/align_v2_checks.py

Appendix A — Figures

Figure A1. Binary flood mask (data/processed/flood_mask.tif) over the study area. The 47 km² of detected pixels are scattered across the whole 1.5° × 1.0° mosaic and do not follow the Trishuli / Bhote Koshi corridor. This is the negative result in one image.

Figure A2. EMSR927 AOIs (colored outlines) over the post-event VV backscatter. The four AOIs cover the GLOF-affected corridor, but the SAR imagery is dominated by terrain rather than a flood signature.

Figure A3. Median VV backscatter change per AOI, compared against the expected GLOF signature band (−5 to −10 dB, green shaded). Every AOI sits within ±0.5 dB of zero — the signal is not in the data.

Figure A4. U-Net training history on Sen1Floods11. Loss decreases monotonically; validation IoU peaks at 0.523 (epoch 6) and then oscillates — the model has converged on a 252-chip dataset.

Figure A5. Damage overcount. Our flood-driven pipeline flags 61,977 buildings; EMSR927 mapped 3,816 damaged structures. The 16× gap quantifies that the SAR mask driving our impact layer is noise.

Figure A6. Per-AOI EMSR927 validation. Destroyed-building recall is zero at both Rasuwa AOIs (Syapru Besi, Timure) — the locations where the GLOF actually occurred.

Situation report (EN)

Situation Report — Trishuli / Bhote Koshi GLOF

Event: 26 August 2026 flash flood (suspected GLOF), Rasuwa District, Nepal Report date: 2026-10-02 Issued by: Trishuli Flood Damage Mapping project (Track B, Multimodal AI Hackathon 2026) Status: Post-event analysis — negative-result on satellite flood detection

1. Situation

On 26 August 2026 a debris-laden flash flood struck the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridor draining south from the Nepal–China border. The Copernicus EMS Rapid Mapping service was activated (EMSR927) and mapped building damage in four Areas of Interest (AOIs):

  • AOI01 Syapru Besi (Rasuwa) — 433 damaged structures
  • AOI02 Timure (Rasuwa) — 431 damaged structures
  • AOI03 Bidur (Nuwakot) — 2,343 damaged structures
  • AOI05 Phosretar (Chitwan edge) — 609 damaged structures

Total: 3,816 damaged structures (2,813 Destroyed, 354 Damaged, 649 Possibly damaged).

2. Key finding

The available Sentinel-1 SAR imagery does not contain the flood signal.

  • Pre-event: 2026-08-16, post-event: 2026-08-28 (relOrbit 85, ascending).
  • Median VV backscatter change across all four AOIs: −0.31 to +0.41 dB. A real flood over water produces −5 to −10 dB. The signal is within noise.
  • A U-Net segmentation model trained on Sen1Floods11 independently predicts zero flood pixels across the Rasuwa corridor.

Two independent methods converge on the same conclusion. The pipeline is correct; the data does not resolve the event.

3. What we produced

Deliverable Content Confidence
Flood mask 47 km² scattered wet terrain ⚠️ not the GLOF
Affected bridges 98 bridge features ⚠️ mask-driven
Affected buildings 154,022 features ❌ 16× overcount vs EMSR927
Hospital cut-off 13 settlements with >3× detour ⚠️ mostly sub-km artifacts
U-Net IoU 0.523 (val), 0.554 (proxy-Himalaya) ✅ model is real

4. Limitations

  • Sentinel-1's 12-day repeat and 30 m resolution cannot resolve a fast-draining GLOF in a 30–50 m gorge.
  • The ascending pass illuminates the valley obliquely; deep N–S gorges are partly in radar shadow.
  • EMSR927 GRA products contain no flood extent layer — validation is proxy (building damage points and landslide overlap).
  • OSM snapshot is post-event (2026-09-30), contaminating the pre-flood infrastructure baseline.

5. Recommendations

  1. Re-acquire with optical imagery (Sentinel-2, PlanetScope) for sediment plumes, or with high-resolution SAR (TerraSAR-X) to resolve the channel.
  2. Try the descending-pass Sentinel-1 scenes (relOrbit 121 or 19) if a shorter revisit becomes available.
  3. For future GLOF events, task optical assets within 24–72 hours — the Sentinel-1 repeat cycle is too slow.
  4. Fix the debris-mask classifier before re-use (currently speckle-dominated).

6. Data sources

  • Sentinel-1 GRD (Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem) — relOrbit 85, ascending.
  • Copernicus EMS Rapid Mapping — activation EMSR927.
  • OpenStreetMap (ODbL) — buildings, roads, hospitals, settlements.
  • Copernicus DEM / SRTM — 30 m slope mask.
  • Sen1Floods11 v1.1 (CC BY 4.0) — U-Net training.

Full attribution: ATTRIBUTION.md. Full analysis: FINAL_REPORT.md.

README

Trishuli Flood Damage Mapping

Track B — Multimodal AI Hackathon 2026

Post-event damage assessment for the 26 August 2026 Trishuli–Bhote Koshi flash flood (Rasuwa District, Nepal) using free Sentinel-1 SAR, DEM, OpenStreetMap, and Copernicus EMS Rapid Mapping reference data.

Headline finding. The Sentinel-1 pre/post pair available for this event (2026-08-16 / 2026-08-28, relOrbit 85, ascending) does not contain the GLOF signal. Two independent methods — a physics-based SAR change detector and a U-Net segmentation model — both return effectively zero flood on the Rasuwa corridor. The pipeline is correct; the data does not resolve the event. See outputs/diagnostics/ and FINAL_REPORT.md.

Pipeline

fetch (S1 + OSM) -> geocode S1 -> align (30 m UTM 45N) -> detect (SAR)
    -> damage (OSM intersect) -> cutoff (hospital reachability)
    -> validate (EMSR927) -> sanity checks -> report
Stage Script Output
S1 download src/fetch/fetch_sentinel1.py data/raw/s1/{pre,post}/*.SAFE
OSM download src/download/fetch_osm.py data/raw/osm/*.geojson
Geocode src/processing/geocode_s1.py data/raw/s1/*/geocoded/*.tif
Align src/processing/align.py data/processed/s1_*_30m.tif
Orbit check src/processing/align_v2_checks.py (validation gate)
Flood detect src/processing/flood_detect_v2.py data/processed/flood_mask.tif
Damage src/processing/damage_v2.py outputs/affected_*.geojson
Cutoff src/processing/cutoff_v2.py outputs/cutoff_settlements.json
Train U-Net src/modeling/train_segmentation.py outputs/flood_unet.pt
Eval U-Net src/modeling/eval_himalaya_heldout.py outputs/himalaya_heldout_metrics.json
EMSR927 validation src/validation/emsr927_comparison.py data/processed/emsr927_comparison.json
Damage sanity src/validation/damage_sanity_check.py outputs/validation/damage_sanity.json

Setup

python3 -m venv ~/flood-venv
source ~/flood-venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

Set credentials in src/config.py:

COPERNICUS_USER = "you@example.com"
COPERNICUS_PASS = "your-password"

Register free at https://dataspace.copernicus.eu/. src/config.py is .gitignored to prevent accidental commits.

Run

bash run_all.sh

or step-by-step (see Pipeline table above).

Train / eval U-Net

python -m src.modeling.train_segmentation      # ~2.5 h CPU, 20 epochs
python src/modeling/eval_himalaya_heldout.py   # ~5 min

Trained on Sen1Floods11 v1.1 (252 train / 89 val). Best val IoU 0.523, final F1 0.593. Proxy-Himalaya (India + Pakistan) IoU 0.554.

U-Net Rasuwa flood fraction 0.000

Papers referenced for threshold justification

  • Twele, A., Cao, W., Plank, S., Martinis, S. (2016). Sentinel-1-based flood mapping: a fully automated processing chain, Int. J. Remote Sensing 37(13), 2990-3004. (Basis for -1.5 dB change threshold.)
  • Lee, J.-S. (1980). Digital image enhancement and noise filtering by use of local statistics, IEEE TPAMI. (Lee speckle filter.)
  • Otsu, N. (1979). A threshold selection method from gray-level histograms, IEEE SMC. (Adaptive thresholding.)
  • Ronneberger, O., Fischer, P., Brox, T. (2015). U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation, MICCAI. (Model architecture.)
